mr_title: refactor: Update _log_transaction_async to be asynchronous and improve task management
mr_description:
- Changed _log_transaction_async method from synchronous to asynchronous to allow proper handling of transaction logging.
- Added error handling for task cancellation and ensured that pending tasks are managed correctly.
- Updated calls to _log_transaction_async in the ComponentVertex class to await the asynchronous method, ensuring proper flow execution and error handling.

expected_issues.title: Deadlock risk: This method is called by `_get_result`, which is invoked by `get_result` i…
expected_issues.description:
Deadlock risk: This method is called by `_get_result`, which is invoked by `get_result` inside an `async with self._lock:` block. Attempting to acquire `self._lock` again here will cause a deadlock because `asyncio.Lock` is not reentrant. 

Additionally, awaiting `asyncio.gather(*tasks)` inside the lock serializes logging and blocks the vertex execution until previous logs are processed, which may significantly impact performance.
expected_issues.source_text:

expected_issues.title: There is a logical error in the outer `asyncio.CancelledError` exception handler
expected_issues.description: There is a logical error in the outer `asyncio.CancelledError` exception handler. The inner code clears `self.log_transaction_tasks` before calling `asyncio.gather(*tasks)`, so when a `CancelledError` is caught in the outer handler, `self.log_transaction_tasks` is already empty. The outer handler iterates over `self.log_transaction_tasks` instead of the local `tasks` variable, meaning no pending tasks will be cancelled when an error occurs from the outer context.

known_false_positives.description: The try-except block for `asyncio.CancelledError` around `asyncio.gather` is redundant because cancellation is automatically propagated to all pending tasks by `asyncio.gather` per Python's documentation. Remove the unnecessary exception handling.

The added `CancelledError` handling in `_log_transaction_async` is unnecessary because the exception would only occur if the current task is cancelled (not due to task completion), making manual task cancellation redundant; the actual unhandled `CancelledError` originates from `task.result()` calls in `chat.py`.
